title: The Telephone
tagline: From Bell’s first call to the smartphone.
source: Generated from “Timeline of the telephone” on Wikipedia; each event links to its source article.

events.title: Robert Hooke
events.text: Robert Hooke creates an acoustic string telephone that conveys sounds over a taut extended wire by mechanical vibrations.

events.title: Reis telephone
events.text: Johann Philipp Reis transfers voice electrically over a distance of 340 feet with his Reis telephone. To prove that speech can be recognized successfully at the receiving end, he uses the phrase "The horse does not eat cucumber salad" as an example b

events.title: Alexander Graham Bell
events.text: Alexander Graham Bell conceives the theoretical concept for the telephone while vacationing at his parents' farm near Brantford, Ontario, Canada. Alexander Melville Bell records notes of his son's conversation in his personal journal.

events.title: acoustic telegraphy
events.text: Thomas Edison experiments with acoustic telegraphy and, in November, builds an electro-dynamic receiver but does not exploit it.

events.title: carbon microphone
events.text: Edison tests his first carbon microphone.

events.title: Edison "first [succeeds] in transmitting over wires many articulated s
events.text: Edison "first [succeeds] in transmitting over wires many articulated sentences" using carbon granules as a pressure-sensitive varying resistance under the pressure of a diaphragm.

references.label: Encyclopedia article: Timeline of the telephone

events.title: Bell Telephone Company
events.text: The Bell Telephone Company, a common law joint-stock company, is organized by Alexander Graham Bell's future father-in-law Gardiner Greene Hubbard, a lawyer who becomes its first president.

events.title: the Bell Telephone Company sues Western Union for infringing Bell's pa
events.text: the Bell Telephone Company sues Western Union for infringing Bell's patents.

references.label: Encyclopedia article: Timeline of the telephone

events.title: Bell Telephone Company
events.text: Early months of 1879: The Bell Telephone Company is near bankruptcy and desperate to get a transmitter to equal Edison's carbon transmitter.

events.title: Sydney
events.text: The Sydney telephone exchange opened with 12 subscribers.

events.title: American Telephone & Telegraph Company
events.text: The American Telephone & Telegraph Company (AT&T) is incorporated as the long-distance division of American Bell Telephone Company. It will become the head of the Bell System on the last day of 1899.

events.title: AT&T becomes the overall holding company for all the Bell companies
events.text: AT&T becomes the overall holding company for all the Bell companies.

references.label: Encyclopedia article: Timeline of the telephone

events.title: American Bell Telephone Company
events.text: American Bell Telephone Company is purchased by its own long-distance subsidiary, American Telephone and Telegraph (AT&T) to bypass state regulations limiting capitalization. AT&T assumes leadership role of the Bell System.

events.title: First transmission of speech across the Atlantic Ocean by radiotelepho
events.text: First transmission of speech across the Atlantic Ocean by radiotelephone from Arlington, Virginia to Paris, France.

references.label: Encyclopedia article: Timeline of the telephone

events.title: Alexander Graham Bell
events.text: For only the second time in history, telephone lines were halted for one minute across the United States, on the day of the death of Alexander Graham Bell, inventor of the telephone.

events.title: Opening of commercial ship-to-shore telephone service
events.text: Opening of commercial ship-to-shore telephone service.

references.label: Encyclopedia article: Timeline of the telephone

events.title: Multi-frequency
events.text: Multi-frequency dialing introduced for operators in Baltimore, Maryland

events.title: Phil Porter, a Bell Labs engineer, proposed that cell towers be at the
events.text: Phil Porter, a Bell Labs engineer, proposed that cell towers be at the corners of the hexagons rather than the centers and have directional antennas pointing in 3 directions.

references.label: Encyclopedia article: Timeline of the telephone

events.title: Mohamed Atalla
events.text: Following Frosch and Derick research at Bell Labs, Mohamed Atalla and Dawon Kahng proposed a silicon MOS transistor in 1959 at Bell Labs.

events.title: Touch-Tone
events.text: Initiation of Touch-Tone service trials

events.title: electronic switching system
events.text: The world's first electronic switching system commences commercial service in Succasunna, New Jersey, in form of the 1ESS.

events.title: touch-tone
events.text: Bell Labs combined MOS technology with touch-tone technology to develop a push-button MOS touch-tone phone called the "Touch-O-Matic" telephone, which uses MOS integrated circuit chips and could store up to 32 phone numbers.

events.title: NMT
events.text: World's first NMT phone call in Tampere, Finland.

events.title: FCC approved AT&T proposal for AMPS and allocated frequencies in the 8
events.text: FCC approved AT&T proposal for AMPS and allocated frequencies in the 824–894 MHz band.

events.title: Mink, Louisiana
events.text: Mink, Louisiana, finally receives traditional landline telephone service (one of the last in the United States).
